name: Workato
description: Workato is an enterprise integration and automation platform that connects SaaS and on-premises systems, automates cross-department workflows, and orchestrates AI agents.
best_for: Enterprise IT, finance, HR, and revenue operations teams that need deep, governed integrations across many business systems and AI agents.
features: 500+ pre-built connectors for enterprise apps like Salesforce, NetSuite, Workday, and ServiceNow
Agent Studio for building custom AI agents plus pre-built "Workato Genies" for IT, Sales, HR, and Support
MCP Gateway for governed Model Context Protocol tool access
Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) and Data Hub / master data management
Built-in API management and B2B/EDI capabilities
Robotic process automation for legacy system tasks
Regional cloud instances (US, EU, Singapore, Japan, Korea, Australia, Israel) for data residency

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.notes: Entry platform edition: app integration & process automation, recipe lifecycle management, dev/test/prod environments, 1 Standard Workbot, SAML SSO/MFA, encryption at rest/transit, 30-day log retention, 1 concurrency. No public price listed. Billing basis: not publicly stated.

tiers.name: Business MCP
tiers.notes: Everything in Standard plus pre-built MCP servers, AI/MCP Gateway, Enterprise Skill builder, data integration (ETL/ELT/reverse ETL), API platform, 10 Enterprise Workbots, 3 on-prem connectivity agents (OPAs). No public price listed. Billing basis: not publicly stated.

tiers.name: Enterprise MCP
tiers.notes: Everything in Business MCP plus Data Pipelines, Event Streams, Intelligent Document Processing, AI by Workato, Insights, unlimited Enterprise Workbots, enhanced security, 90-day log retention, 10 OPAs, 15 concurrency. No public price listed. Billing basis: not publicly stated.

tiers.name: Workato ONE
tiers.notes: Top edition: everything in Enterprise MCP plus Agent Studio, Workato Knowledge Base, Workato GO (Employee Assistant, Enterprise Search, Action Board), 30 OPAs, 30 concurrency. No public price listed. Billing basis: not publicly stated.

cons: No public list pricing exists anywhere on the official site: all four platform editions (Standard, Business MCP, Enterprise MCP, Workato ONE) are gated behind "Schedule a demo" / "Get a quote" with the page itself stating pricing "may vary based on your contract terms" -- combined with usage/task-based billing, this makes costs impossible to know upfront, and third-party review aggregation (G2, cited via Integrate.io's review) reports buyers seeing automation costs "doubling within 6-12 months" as task volume grows.

The platform has documented hard caps on data-handling that make it a poor fit for heavy ETL/data-pipeline use: CSV parsing is capped at 50,000 records and the Lookup Table feature maxes out at 100,000 rows, reflecting that Workato is built primarily for business-process/app integration rather than purpose-built data transformation -- teams needing complex joins, data masking, or deduplication hit these ceilings.

There is no self-serve, ongoing free plan: the official pricing page's only calls-to-action are demo/quote requests (no listed free tier), so unlike self-serve iPaaS competitors (e.g., Zapier, Airbyte), evaluating Workato requires a sales-assisted trial or demo rather than an instant sign-up with published usage limits.
